questions.q: What happens to an invoice's status when you edit a distribution after it has already reached Validated?
options: Nothing changes; the edit is silently accepted
The invoice is automatically cancelled
The status resets to Needs Revalidation, requiring the Validate action to run again
The invoice is automatically approved
questions.explain: Editing a validated invoice knocks its invoice status back to Needs Revalidation until it is re-checked.

questions.q: At which stage is an invoice generally the MOST flexible to adjust?
options: After it has been paid
After it has been accounted but before payment
There is no difference between any stage
After it has been validated but before it is accounted
questions.explain: Validated-but-unaccounted invoices are the most flexible, since only Payables itself has acted on them so far.

questions.q: What is Payables' default behavior regarding distributions on a paid or partially paid invoice?
options: They are normally prevented from being updated or reversed, since the payment was built from that accounting
They can always be freely edited
They are automatically deleted
They can only be edited by the supplier
questions.explain: By default, Payables blocks changes to distributions on paid/partially paid invoices, because the payment already reflects that accounting.

questions.q: Why does Payables restrict edits more heavily as an invoice progresses from validated to accounted to paid?
options: Because Oracle arbitrarily disables more buttons over time
Because later stages have more systems or records (ledger postings, actual payments) that already depend on the invoice looking a certain way
Because invoice numbers change at each stage
Because suppliers are not allowed to see paid invoices
questions.explain: Each later stage has more downstream dependents (journal postings, an actual payment) that a silent change would disconnect from reality.

questions.q: If a miscoded distribution is discovered only AFTER an invoice has already been paid, what does correcting it generally require?
options: A simple edit to the distribution, same as before payment
Nothing — paid invoices cannot have accounting issues
Re-entering the invoice number
Reversal or adjustment tools, rather than a direct edit
questions.explain: Once paid, a direct edit is normally blocked, so correcting the issue requires the reversal/adjustment mechanisms covered in the next lesson.
